title: Live Tournament
subtitle: Keeping a session honest while it is still moving.

hero.alt: A live session showing progress, the current round and who is sitting out

intro: A tournament on paper assumes everyone who signed up turns up, stays fit and leaves at the end. Real sessions do none of that: people arrive late, roll an ankle, take a call, or have to go at six.

These are the controls for the middle of a session — pausing a player, bringing them back, standing someone in, taking someone out — designed so that using them does not corrupt the results already recorded.
bestfor: Drop-in sessions where the player list changes as the evening goes on
Organisers who have had to redraw a schedule by hand mid-event
Anyone running a session while also playing in it

sections.title: Sitting a round out
sections.text: A break is not the same as leaving. TournaQ keeps a player's place and their points, and puts them back where they were.

cards.h: Choose who, and for how long
cards.p: Pick the player and whether they are out for this round only or until you bring them back. Everything they have already banked stays with them.
cards.alt: The break picker for choosing which player sits out and for how long

cards.p: Their spot becomes an anonymous placeholder so anyone courtside can step in, and nothing else is reshuffled — the rest of the draw is untouched.
cards.alt: A dialog explaining that a player's seat becomes a placeholder while they are on a break

cards.p: Return them and they slot back into the rotation. Nobody else's position moves, and the schedule does not have to be rebuilt.
cards.alt: A dialog bringing a player back from a break

sections.title: Someone steps in
sections.text: An open seat should not stop a court. Somebody courtside can take it for the round.

cards.h: A stand-in on a live court
cards.p: The placeholder left by a break or an ejection can be filled by whoever is available, so the round runs on time instead of playing three against four while you find somebody.
cards.alt: A stand-in occupying an open seat on a live court

cards.p: In the rotation formats, the pair due on next can be swapped by hand — for the player still tying a shoelace, or the one who has just walked in.
cards.alt: A dialog for swapping the challenging pair by hand

sections.title: Someone has to leave
sections.text: The hard case. A player going home mid-session has to be handled without invalidating the evening so far.

p: Re-pair the remaining rounds without them, or leave their seat as a placeholder so nobody else's pairings move. TournaQ asks which you want rather than choosing for you, because the right answer depends on how much of the session is left.
Either way, the games they have already played still count towards the ranking.
cards.alt: A dialog asking whether to re-pair the remaining rounds or leave the departing player's seat open

cards.h: The player list is the control panel
cards.p: Everyone in the session with their games and points, and on each row the four things you need mid-evening: pause, rename, swap, remove.
cards.alt: The player sheet listing everyone with games played, points and per-player actions
